title: A comic peddler who led the second line
summary: Rene describes a jolly barefoot peddler whose dance steps the second line followed like a grand marshal.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Who was that second liner that was a peddler or something too that you were telling me about?

That's the fellow there I never could get. He was a star fellow. Sometimes that guy would go behind the second line barefooted man. That's his star, he liked his music you know. I forgot, he was right from the third wall just. He was a kind of a jolly fellow you know. He was a bad man you know. He used to peddle. And I can't call his name. But boy he the one used to do what they called a duck you know. Used to do that then. Wave his hands in water. Yeah, wave his hands in water. Then he would back up you know. Then he would go forward. Then the second line would fall right on in with it. Oh he would take the lead man. He was out. I would consider him as being a grand marshal in the second line. Cause whatever he'd do they would do you see. Yeah, take the lead in that. Very jolly fellow man used to like that. I can't call that fellow man. He was a peddler. Did he carry a broomstick?

He didn't care no broomstick. He didn't care nothing. Sometimes I ain't going to his understreet man. Leave him downtown. Go all the way up top man. In his understreet. Stop everybody but stop and look at him and laugh.
Did he hang out in any particular corner man? Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Where did he hang out man?
Pedile and Grab. Pedile and Grab. I mean Franklin and Grab.
Could ask somebody from that neighborhood they might know him. Yeah. I guess he's gone now.
Oh I guess he's gone now. I can't go off. He was a sort of good nature fellow you know. But he was just naturally one of them comical fellows you know.
Well they wouldn't fight in the second line would they?
